purpose: Period/cult/text atlas for ancient Egyptian, Mesopotamian, Greek and Roman religions. Prevents modern denomination logic and literary mythology from replacing lived cult, ritual, archaeology and institutional history.
rules: Ancient religion pages organize by period, place, cult, ritual and source type rather than founder/denomination.
A literary mythology source does not by itself describe the full lived religion of a society.
A god-name shared or equated across cultures does not prove identity or unchanged continuity.
Afterlife, underworld, kingship, sacrifice, mystery initiation and household religion remain typed separately.
Modern project comparisons stay downstream of native-context explanation.

traditions.title: Ancient Egyptian religion

source_strata.name: Coffin Texts
source_strata.job: expanded funerary texts on coffins; includes Book of Two Ways cosmography

source_strata.name: Book of the Dead / Book of Going Forth by Day
source_strata.job: portable funerary spell collections; not a single fixed canonical book

cautions: Do not reduce Egyptian religion to the Book of the Dead.
Do not treat all Egyptian deities as a timeless fixed pantheon.
Ma'at is principle/order as well as divine personification in different contexts.

traditions.title: Ancient Mesopotamian religions
traditions.historical_span: late 4th millennium BCE through early centuries CE
cautions: Do not create one timeless 'Mesopotamian pantheon'.
Sumerian, Akkadian, Babylonian and Assyrian traditions overlap but change by city, period and empire.
Temple is literally conceptualized as the god's house in major traditions; cult statue, offering and city identity matter.

traditions.title: Ancient Greek religion
traditions.historical_span: Bronze Age antecedents through Hellenistic/Roman Greek worlds
cautions: Homer and Hesiod are influential literary sources, not a Greek Bible.
Cult practice is local and polis-specific.
Mystery cults are diverse and should not be reconstructed as one secret religion.

traditions.title: Ancient Roman religion
traditions.historical_span: Republican antecedents through late Roman empire
cautions: Roman religion is not simply Greek mythology translated into Latin names.
Household religion and civic religion are both central.
Imperial cult varies by place and period and should not be reduced to emperors 'claiming to be gods' in one uniform way.

source_notes.note: Pyramid Texts → Coffin Texts → Book of the Dead sequence used as public orientation; deeper source work should prefer Egyptological editions and museum/academic corpora.
Temple as divine house, city-state religion and long historical span are central organizing facts.
Sacrifice, sanctuaries, festivals, oracles and mysteries establish that lived Greek religion is larger than literary mythology.
Civic ritual, household Lares/Penates, divination, imperial cult and imported cults require separate layers.
